title: Cure Deposit after Returned Payments on the RentGuard Renters Policy
content:
A RentGuard Renters Policy cancelled for nonpayment whose payments were returned unpaid by the bank in the last 12 calendar months carries a deposit in the cure.

## Standard

1. When two or more renters payments were returned unpaid in the last 12 calendar months, a deposit of one scheduled installment (1 times the scheduled installment) is added to the cure.
2. When exactly one renters payment was returned unpaid in the last 12 calendar months, a deposit of half of one scheduled installment (0.5 times the scheduled installment) is added to the cure.
3. When no renters payment was returned unpaid in the last 12 calendar months, no deposit is added.

A scheduled installment is taken at the amount of the latest installment billed on the policy. A deposit stays on the account as a credit toward the installments that follow.

## Records read

- Returned payments: the entries on the RentGuard premium account recording a payment returned unpaid by the bank, counted when posted within the last 12 calendar months. A return posted earlier than that is not counted.
- Scheduled installment: the amount of the installment billed most recently on the premium account.

| Returned payments in the last 12 calendar months | Deposit added to the cure |
|---|---|
| 0 | none |
| 1 | half of one scheduled installment |
| 2 | one scheduled installment |
| 3 or more | one scheduled installment |

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

For a hypothetical policy whose latest installment billed is 21.40:

- two returned payments in the last 12 calendar months: a deposit of 21.40;
- one returned payment: a deposit of 10.70;
- no returned payment: no deposit.

In each case the deposit, once paid, remains on the account as a credit toward the installments that follow.
